framing.simulated_expert: Derm7pt's ground-truth 7-point criteria stand in for a SIMULATED expert supplying corrections. This is standard correctability / active-feature-acquisition methodology, NOT a human study -- no clinician judgement is involved in generating these corrections.
framing.predicted_criteria_source: argmax of the frozen per-criterion heads (medguard_v2.pipeline.run_cohort.fit_readers), fit on Derm7pt train only, applied to test. No abstention gating on this starting point -- every criterion has a determinate predicted value, matching the existing scripts/dev/build_loco_analysis.py precedent.
framing.ground_truth_verdict_definition: score_criteria(true_criteria).meets_threshold: the melanoma-suspicion verdict (score>=3) computed from Derm7pt's gold 7-point criteria. By construction this is exactly what every policy reaches at k=7 (values == true_criteria once all 7 are revealed) -- see sanity_checks, not a reported finding.
framing.positive_class: ground_truth_verdict == True, i.e. the fully-informed checklist recommends excision. Sensitivity/specificity below are relative to THIS target, not to the raw melanoma/non-melanoma diagnosis label -- see dataset_property_aside_checklist_vs_diagnosis for that separate comparison.
framing.ordering_policies_are_truth_blind: All three policies choose WHICH criterion to correct next using only already-known information (current partial criteria state, or the head's own confidence); only the reveal step uses the true value of the chosen criterion. None of the policies can 'peek' at ground truth to decide what to correct.

boundaries.abstention_policy_used_for: uncertainty_guided ordering only (per-case margins via AbstentionPolicy.apply); NOT used to gate the k=0 starting criteria

hinge_guided.description: Adaptive: at every step, correct the remaining criterion that verdict_hinges/leave_one_criterion_out currently flags as flipping or undeciding the verdict (largest point weight first among hinges; largest point weight among all remaining when no hinge remains).

uncertainty_guided.description: Fixed per-case order: ascending head margin (top-minus-second posterior), least-confident criterion corrected first.

random.description: 20 independent seeded per-case random permutations; mean +/- std across the replicate-level cohort curves.

hinge_gated_uncertainty_ranked.description: Combined, adaptive. At every step: GATE the remaining candidates to the current LOCO hinges (verdict_hinges intersected with what's left); RANK within that gated set by ascending head margin (most uncertain hinge first). Falls back to ranking ALL remaining criteria by margin (i.e. the same per-step choice uncertainty_guided would make) when no remaining criterion is currently a hinge. Tests: is the best correction target a criterion that is BOTH decision-fragile AND model-uncertain?

uncertainty_gated_hinge_ranked.description: Combined, adaptive, the mirror of hinge_gated_uncertainty_ranked (brief left its exact construction underspecified -- 'the mirror, for completeness'). At every step: GATE the remaining candidates to criteria whose margin is below THEIR OWN fitted abstention threshold (AbstentionPolicy.margins[name] from criterion_abstention_v1.json, reused here as a gate rather than a continuous score); RANK within that gated set by hinge status first (hinge before non-hinge, ties by point weight, then margin ascending). Falls back to the same hinge-first ranking over ALL remaining criteria when nothing clears its own uncertainty gate -- note two criteria (blue_whitish_veil, vascular_structures) have a fitted threshold of exactly 0.0 and so can NEVER clear this gate; see uncertainty_gate_nonempty_fraction_of_steps for how often the gate bound at all across the other five.

already_correct_at_k0.note: Policy-independent: no correction has been applied yet, so this is identical across all three policies (asserted).

hinge_vs_random_area_between_curves.definition: Per-case ABC = mean_k(1{hinge verdict_k correct}) - mean_k(mean over 20 replicates of 1{random verdict_k correct}), k=0..7. Point estimate = mean over cases. Positive means the hinge-guided curve sits above the random-mean curve on average across the correction budget.

hinge_vs_uncertainty_area_between_curves.definition: Same construction as hinge_vs_random, comparing hinge-guided against the uncertainty-guided (head-margin) policy instead of random. Not requested by the core protocol; included because it is nearly free given the same machinery and directly informs whether hinge-guidance beats the next-best truth-blind alternative, not just a naive baseline.

combined_policy_comparisons.note: Follow-up requested by the coordinator after the first pass of this script: does combining hinge-fragility and model-uncertainty beat either signal alone? The core hypothesis test is hinge_gated_uncertainty_ranked_vs_uncertainty_guided -- if that excludes zero in the combined policy's favour, gating hinges by uncertainty is a real win and a directive to rank the renderer's hinge line by model uncertainty. All six comparisons use the same case-resampling bootstrap as hinge_vs_random above (2000 reps, seed 20260810, independently spawned child seeds so they don't perturb the three single-signal policies' own numbers).

dataset_property_aside_checklist_vs_diag.description: NOT a function of k. Compares the FULLY-INFORMED checklist verdict (score_criteria(true_criteria).meets_threshold, i.e. what every policy converges to at k=7) against the actual diagnosis label (diagnosis_group == 'MEL'), on test. This is the real 'ceiling' question: does the 7-point rule, even with perfect criteria knowledge, agree with the pathology label? It is the test-split analogue of G2's oracle-criteria melanoma-detection ceiling (research/evidence/derm7pt_v1/g2_criteria_ceiling.json), which measured sensitivity 0.9016 / specificity 0.8592 on valid with gold criteria feeding the same unlearned published rule.
dataset_property_aside_checklist_vs_diag.reinterpretation_note: The brief that spawned this script asked for 'fraction never correctable within 7 (ground-truth verdict differs even with all criteria corrected)'. Read literally against this protocol's own ground_truth_verdict definition that fraction is tautologically always 0 -- at k=7 the working criteria ARE the true criteria, so the computed verdict cannot differ from itself (see sanity_checks). The substantive, non-tautological version of that question -- does the checklist rule itself disagree with the independent diagnosis label, even fully informed -- is answered above instead, and is the one that ties to a rough-set-style checklist-vs-diagnosis ceiling. That external '92.1%' figure was not found anywhere in this repository (grepped; likely a literature figure from outside this codebase) and is therefore not asserted to match the number computed here -- treat this block as the honest, independently computed analogue, not a reproduction of that specific citation.
